summary: MacBook Pro sleep/resume: VPN does not re-establish reliably, DNS resolution fails for internal hosts
description: Issue summary: Several employees on MacBook Pro M1 (macOS 13.5/14.0) report that after closing the lid or sleeping the machine and re-opening, the corporate WireGuard VPN (wg0) appears connected but internal hostnames (e.g., internal-api.redwood, grafana.corp) fail to resolve or connections time out. Impact: Impairs access to internal tooling (CI, logs, internal docs) for engineers returning from meetings. Multiple reports from US-West office, intermittent but frequent (3–5 times per day for affected users). Environment: Corporate Wi-Fi (802.11ax, enterprise WPA2/3), WireGuard-based corporate VPN (wg0) terminating at wireguard-gateway-1 in us-west, affected clients are Apple Silicon MacBook Pro 14/16" (2021/2023) running macOS 13.5 and early 14.0 builds. Observed behavior: After resume, 'wg' shows interface up and handshake recent, but DNS queries for internal domains either return NXDOMAIN or time out. Some users see traffic routed directly to WAN (split tunnel) rather than being forced through VPN until a manual reconnect. Expected behavior: VPN stays connected (or automatically re-negotiates) and internal DNS resolution works immediately after wake with no user action required.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Connect to corporate Wi-Fi and establish WireGuard (wg0) VPN.
2) Access an internal hostname (curl https://internal-api.redwood) — observe success.
3) Close lid / let Mac sleep for ~30s to 5min.
4) Reopen lid and attempt to access same internal hostname.
5) Observe DNS failures (NXDOMAIN or timeout) or long hang followed by direct connection failure.

investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): verified pattern tied to macOS sleep/resume and mostly Apple Silicon models; Windows/Linux not reporting.
Hypothesis 1: macOS resolver order or mDNSResponder not reinitializing VPN DNS server entries after sleep, so system falls back to Wi-Fi AP DNS (192.168.1.1) which cannot resolve internal zones.

Hypothesis 2: WireGuard reports interface 'up' (kernel device present) but routing rules or PF rules that force default route through wg0 are not reinstalled on resume — traffic egresses via local gateway.
Collected packet capture from affected machine during reproduce: DNS queries observed going to 192.168.1.1 instead of 10.11.0.2; no SYNs seen to internal-api until manual wg-quick restart.
Checked server-side: gateway shows active handshake timestamps; no session terminations logged; server ACLs accept traffic when it arrives.
Reproduced on dev MacBook Pro M1: confirmed scutil lost the VPN nameserver entry after wake (resolver order changed). Restarting mDNSResponder re-populates entries in some cases.
Related: INT-4312 showed MTU/fragmentation around VPN over Wi-Fi; not the same root cause but may increase symptom frequency when packet loss is present.
temporary_workarounds: 1) Toggle Wi-Fi off and on (fastest user fix).
2) Run 'sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder' which in many cases restores resolver entries.
3) Reconnect WireGuard: 'sudo wg-quick down wg0 && sudo wg-quick up wg0' — guarantees routing/DNS entries are reinstalled.
4) If urgent, tether via phone hotspot (bypasses problematic AP DNS).

next_steps: 1) QA: reproduce on 3 different M1/M2 machines with macOS 13.5 and 14.0 and test variants (sleep lid vs standby).

2) Implement and dogfood a wake hook (launchd/com.apple.logind) that runs a short script: validate scutil resolver, HUP mDNSResponder, and restart wg(quick) if the resolver for redwood.corp is missing.
3) Validate server-side whether enforcing DNS via push-options (if supported) can be relied upon — evaluate WG options vs. local resolver plumbing.
4) If reproducible, open an Apple bug (Feedback Assistant) with logs and sysdiagnose; escalate if intermittent regression is confirmed across macOS builds.
5) Document permanent mitigation and push KB to internal IT help center.
resolution: In progress — temporary mitigations documented. Engineering to validate and deploy wake-script to affected machines and file bug with Apple if reproduction is stable. Final resolution pending QA of script and potential server-side config changes.
final_notes: If wake-script proves reliable, rollout via Jamf policy for macOS fleet and add monitoring alert to detect post-sleep DNS failures (synthetic probe user-level).
